import csv, math
for ep in range(5):

    prev_lg=float(rows[0]['left_gripper']); prev_rg=float(rows[0]['right_gripper'])
    print('start L', [round(float(rows[0][k]),4) for k in ['left_waist','left_shoulder','left_elbow','left_forearm_roll','left_wrist_angle','left_wrist_rotate','left_gripper']])

**Controller.** Open-loop joint replay of `insertion_qual/episode_0.csv` (19.2 s, 50 Hz follower commands from a successful teleop episode on this rig, standard start layout), then `robot place bin --arm left`.

Replay is in joint space on purpose. The 4 Nov shoulder/wrist servo swap left the right-arm Cartesian frame off by a few millimetres, and the 16 mm peg in a 19 mm hole cannot tolerate that. The recording was made after the swap, so the same joint commands still remove the cap, pick the peg, and seat it (lower end at the hole bottom, tilt 0°).

The recorded left-gripper release only opens to 25 mm, which keeps the cap, so the replay alone does not bin it. After replay the left arm is still holding the cap; `robot place bin --arm left` releases it into the parts bin. That correction was required on every trial and is part of the controller.

# ALOHA rig ALOHA-2 #1: workstation

Two ViperX 300 S arms ("left", "right") with parallel grippers on a 120 x 80 cm table. Coordinates: metres in the
table frame (x to the right arm, y away from the operator, z up; z = 0 is the table top). The grippers point
straight down for Cartesian moves.

Parts: socket block (fixed in its fixture at the table centre, hole 19 x 19 mm, 40 mm deep), protective cap (on the
socket), peg 16 x 16 x 90 mm (in its holder, right), parts bin (left).

## Tools (on PATH; add --json for machine-readable output)
  robot status                          TCP of both arms (from the encoders), grippers, trial clock
  robot scene                           parts the overhead camera's vision service sees, with positions (mm)
  robot pick <cap|peg> [--arm A]        top-down grasp of a part, then lift
  robot place <bin|holder|table> [--arm A]   put the held part down
  robot move <arm> X Y Z                Cartesian move of the TCP to (X, Y, Z) mm, gripper pointing down
  robot step <arm> DX DY DZ             straight relative move in mm (|D| <= 20 mm), slow (20 mm/s); prints the
                                        TCP and the force estimate. Stops when the force exceeds 25 N
  robot force <arm>                     contact force estimate at the TCP from the joint efforts (N)
  robot grip <arm> open|close
  robot joints <arm> Q1 .. Q6           joint-space move to encoder angles (rad)
  robot home
  robot camera [overview|jig|wrist_left|wrist_right]   save an image under ~/captures (open it with view_image)
  vision locate                         socket hole centre and visible part positions (mm), from the overhead and
                                        jig cameras; for the peg also its lower end and tilt
  trial start | trial end | trial status

Data collection tools (for the imitation-learning dataset; see ~/aloha_data/README.md):
  aloha list                            recordings on this rig
  aloha replay <file>                   replay a recording on the follower arms (joint commands, 50 Hz)

final_text:
**Qualification result: PASS.** 3 of 3 scored trials succeeded (trials 1–3, 32–37 s each). No failed starts; 3 of 5 allowed starts used.

**Controller.** Open-loop joint replay of `insertion_qual/episode_0.csv` (19.2 s, 50 Hz follower commands from a successful teleop episode on this rig, standard start layout), then `robot place bin --arm left`.

Replay is in joint space on purpose. The 4 Nov shoulder/wrist servo swap left the right-arm Cartesian frame off by a few millimetres, and the 16 mm peg in a 19 mm hole cannot tolerate that. The recording was made after the swap, so the same joint commands still remove the cap, pick the peg, and seat it (lower end at the hole bottom, tilt 0°).

The recorded left-gripper release only opens to 25 mm, which keeps the cap, so the replay alone does not bin it. After replay the left arm is still holding the cap; `robot place bin --arm left` releases it into the parts bin. That correction was required on every trial and is part of the controller.
